notes:
SE->DX9 vtable slot map for uEnemy-derived classes (SE 144 slots / DX9 103): 0-5 identical, 9->7 moveEx, 11->8 sync, 12->9 draw, 21->12 kill, 50->29, 53->30 main, 54->31 updatePtr, 59->36 damageMessage, 60->37, 63->40, 64->41, 67->44, 68->45, 69->46, 70..73->47..50, 76->51, 82->56, 83->57, 84->58, 90..96->64..70, 106->76, 114->77, 115->78, 116->79, 117->80, 118->81, 125->87, 126->88, 128->89, 136->97, 137->98, 144/145->103/104 (uEm011Test). Shell/uActor classes (SE 114-116 / DX9 77-79) use the same map for the shared prefix. Existing DX9 '::die' at slot 12 is SE kill, 'validateTargetPtrs' is SE updatePtr, uEm012 'damageMessage_2/damageMessage3' are effectMessage/effectMeleeMessage, uEm036 'damageMessage7' (slot 80) is getNearTargetEnemy (decompile-verified) - all renamed with 'was:' in the comment.
DX9 vtable label for uEm036 (0xBD8780) is truncated by a stray label off_BD88AC at slot 75; the real vtable has 103 slots (same layout as other uEnemy-derived classes).
Defined 15 missing functions in-span (all were 'loc_' code): per class the MyDTI::newInstance allocator stub right after getDTI and the vtable slot-0 scalar/vector deleting destructor (0x5b3170,0x5b3640,0x5cec00,0x5cecd0,0x5cfb10,0x5cfcc0,0x5d1b90,0x5dacd0,0x5dad30,0x5db230,0x5db2c0,0x5ef750,0x5efd30,0x723c00,0x7241e0). Destructors named with SE mangled names (??1/??_E/??_G) so the ~ survives.
Action dispatch: uEm012 main dispatches via function table funcs_5D327B (0xE14FF0, 64 entries indexed by action byte [this+0x14]); action setters are 'mov byte [this+0xEA0],N; retn' stubs. Action enum = SE setter TU order with setModeOn/setModeOc reinserted at 29/31 and AttackThunderBolt=52/AttackWeak=53 swapped; verified against every DX9 setter constant and motion-id immediates. Feature/order-only propagation through uEm012 main was WRONG (SE callee lists for table-dispatched functions are address-ordered) and was replaced by this table mapping. Many 18-byte action setters are COMDAT-folded across enemy classes (e.g. 0x5d5420 currently named uEm010::setGrabBlown is uEm012::setDodgeAir and shared with uEm010) - those are commented, not renamed. uEm012::grabBlown is an empty action -> DX9 table slot 46 = nullsub_2.
uEm011/uEm014/uEm011Test/uEm036 main use jump-table switches with direct calls; DX9 case-body layout order equals SE main call order (and TU order), which resolved twin functions (turn90Left/Right, stepSideLeft/Right, uEm036 footwork*/backWalk/surprised/squatsUp/retreatStop). uEm011Test stepRight/stepLeft/stepBack are COMDAT-folded into one DX9 function 0x5d07e0 (cases 3,4,5).
uEm012Dodge: DX9 has no standalone ctor - it is inlined into uEm012::setDodgeEffect (0x5da280, writes uEm012Dodge::vftable) and into MyDTI::newInstance; uEm012Dodge::setParam is 0x5d16f0 (inside the uEm012 code region); dispThunder/dispThunderSub have no DX9 counterpart (inlined into move or absent).
uEm036 is much simpler in DX9: SE path-finding (checkPathFind, walkPath, castRayFunc, setActionByNodeAttr), damage action routines (damage, damageBlown, damageHighTime, damageAir, damageBeatDown, grab*) and postMain have no DX9 functions (postMain inlined into main); DX9 actions are ~150 bytes vs ~420 in SE.
SE-only categories: per-class operator new/new[]/delete x4, usage(), createUI (DX9 uses shared sub_718C00), trivial 3-5 byte message stubs that DX9 resolves to shared nullsubs/uEnemy thunks, most 18-byte setXxx action setters (inlined into setAction switch in uEm011/uEm014/uEm036/uEm011Test, folded in uEm012), setDevilTriggerSign (DX9 slot 79 is inherited sub_701B60), Vergil-era grabLongMessageV, isHighTimeDamage, setShadowQualityCallback.
Remaining DX9-only functions in my regions: see dx_only (e.g. 0x725420 uEm036 helper called from uEm032 and outside the span; 0x5d38f0 probably postEffectCtrlBlur; 0x5da950 maybe searchTarget; 0x5da9c0 / 0x5da850 uncalled helpers).
Global 0xB9A27C is named mInterFrame in DX9 but is the float constant 10.0 (used by uEm012Shl::moveFinalStrike).
